title: British East Africa
capsule: The East Africa Protectorate was a British protectorate established on 1 July 1895 over the territory of the former Imperial British East Africa Company, stretching inland from the Indian Ocean coast (excluding the Sultan of Zanzibar's ten-mile coastal strip) toward the Rift Valley and Lake Victoria. Its development was shaped by the Uganda Railway from Mombasa to Kisumu (1896–1901), which opened the fertile highlands to European settlement and made Nairobi the administrative centre from 1905. After the addition of the Eastern Province transferred from Uganda in 1902, settler agriculture and African resistance defined its early administration. The protectorate was reconstituted as Kenya Colony and Protectorate on 23 July 1920.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Colonial boundary lines in British East Africa were defined by inter-imperial treaties and are well-documented; the dataset entry likely represents a residual administrative or Cliopatria geometry rather than a single coherent polity.
